topic: HarnessEval-W: Agentifying the Evaluation of Visual Worlds

key_points: Introduces HarnessEval-W, an agentified evaluation pipeline bringing the 'harness' paradigm from the LLM ecosystem to world model benchmarking
Instead of a fixed rubric, it interprets each evaluation case, decomposes the question into measurable subproblems, and spawns specialized sub-agents with tailored context and diagnostic tools
Parent agent validates gathered evidence and summarizes into final verdict, producing a transparent evidence tree with a complete reasoning chain
Applied to 18 representative world models over 330 evaluation cases; judgments closely align with human preferences
Authors: Weiliang Chen, Haowen Sun, Jun Gao, Jiawei Chi, Hanyang Wang (MirroS Team); published 2026-08-17
Frames the 'harness' as more than a code wrapper — robust scaffolding to power fully agentic pipelines formalizing human workflows (evidence gathering, tool use, reasoning)
Human evaluation is itself a workflow that can be harnessed; likens the agentic evaluator to Sherlock Holmes discovering clues and connecting evidence
Three evaluation axes: Observation Quality, Transition Correctness, World Persistence

Skill library currently comprises 9 distinct skills (Render Quality, Physical Plausibility, Viewpoint Trajectory, Intentional Change, Physical Response, Physical Dynamics, Drift Degradation, Return Consistency, Offscreen Evolution)
Future directions: test-time scaling for agentic benchmarks, scaling skill libraries, recursive self-improved agentic benchmark
Open-source live benchmark, Apache 2.0 license, ~267 stars, created 2026-08-17
Three conda environments: harnesseval-main (launcher/CLI), harnesseval-metrics (metric backends), harnesseval-pavrm (physical-plausibility backend)
CLI usage: 'harnesseval eval' and 'harnesseval verify run'
Outputs summary.json, leaderboard_latest.json/csv, LEADERBOARD.md per model
Built on VBench (video quality), WBench (world model), WorldScore, Cosmos, Lingbot World, MiniMax H3

Project page with leaderboard-ready reports and benchmark resources

Leaderboard top performers: Seedance 2.0 (75.5 overall), Wan 2.7 (75.0), Kling 3.0 (74.4), MiniMax H3 (74.3), Grok Imagine 1.5 (73.4)
Paper indexed on HuggingFace papers feed
Part of the broader world-model evaluation literature alongside VBench, WBench, and WorldScore
Positions HarnessEval-W against existing brute-force metric benchmarks that lack reasoning chains

stats.fact: HarnessEval-W evaluates 18 representative world models over 330 evaluation cases
Human study collected 5000 A/B pairwise judgments across nine representative models, aggregated via Bradley-Terry model
HarnessEval-W achieves Spearman rank correlation ρ=0.93 (Kendall τ=0.82) with human ordering on Intentional Transition and ρ=0.87 (τ=0.74) on Physical Transition
vs WBench on Physical: pairwise accuracy rises from 31.9% to 71.7%, draw rate cut from 52.2% to 1.8%
vs WBench on Intentional: pairwise accuracy rises from 60.2% to 77.8%, draws fall from 36.1% to 11.1%

Robustness: HarnessEval-W fitted curve slopes stay within 9.6-10.8, correlations with human strength 0.928-0.964, envelope spans only 0.33 Bradley-Terry units; WBench slope nearly doubles (11.2 to 21.0), correlation 0.646-0.780, envelope 1.61 units (4.9x wider)
Skill library comprises 9 distinct skills across the three evaluation axes
Leaderboard top-5 overall: Seedance 2.0 (75.5), Wan 2.7 (75.0), Kling 3.0 (74.4), MiniMax H3 (74.3), Grok Imagine 1.5 (73.4)
GitHub repo MirroS-Lab/HarnessEval-W has ~267 stars, Apache 2.0 license, created 2026-08-17
Scoring policy 'all_families_core_observation_50_50': core weight 0.5, observation weight 0.5

angles: The 'harness' paradigm shift: moving world-model evaluation from brute-force scalar metrics to agentified, evidence-grounded reasoning — borrowed from the LLM ecosystem

Transparent evidence trees: every score backed by an auditable reasoning chain (what was tested, which tool grounded it, the logical chain) — a trust/interpretability differentiator vs black-box benchmarks
Human-alignment as the core validation: 5000 A/B judgments, Spearman ρ=0.93/0.87, and dramatic gains over WBench in pairwise accuracy and draw-rate reduction
Robustness/reproducibility: consistent evaluation across repeated runs (envelope 0.33 vs WBench's 1.61 BT units) — closer to an ideal benchmark
Extensibility as a 'living benchmark': 9-skill library, community-contributed cases and skills, recursive self-improvement vision
Three-axis evaluation framework (Observation Quality / Transition Correctness / World Persistence) as a reusable taxonomy for judging interactive world models
The evaluator-evaluates-the-evaluator angle: robustness under different VLMs and repeated runs
